newsitem.title: UK: IPE gas oil settles higher in dull trade.
newsitem.headline: IPE gas oil settles higher in dull trade.

text.p: IPE May gas oil futures settled 25 cents a tonne higher at $165.25 on Tuesday, shedding off slight losses in earlier trade.

"Pretty unexciting. We had a little bit of a dip during the early sessions of trade then we went back up. The market is basically range-bound. I think overall we still like to think that the market is consolidating at this range," one broker said.
May gas oil hit a low of $164.25 earlier in the day and also a high of $166.50. June gas oil also settled 25 cents higher at $166.25 a tonne.
Traders said the market would be looking for direction on Wedensday from American Petroleum Institute (API) weekly data, due to be released after the markets close on Tuesday.

"Gas oil as a market by itself doesn't have a great deal to say for itself at the moment...It still looks as if the market would like to work a little bit better, a lot of it of course depends on how the APIs turn out tonight," a trader said.
Brent futures continued to trade lower in the late afternoon.
May Brent, which expires at the end of Tuesday's session, was trading 21 cents a barrel down at $17.98 by 1736 GMT.
The June contract was down 12 cents a barrel at $18.22.
Brokers said there was some selling in the market, with two players appearing to sell some 4,000 lots of the Brent June contract, trying to push it down.
Some brokers expected May Brent to expire in the $17.90s or at about $18.00.
One broker said that besides the reports of selling, the market was also pushed down by sentiment that tension between Iran and the West was easing.
